harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired node1’s support-bundle exporter. It now recursively exports regular log files with private permissions, preserves timestamps/event types/ticket IDs, redacts all detected emails and auth_token values, and excludes outward symlinks. Source logs and private.txt remained unchanged. The repair persisted across a verified node reboot without changing RHEL or the kernel.
actions_performed: Replaced bin/export with a RHEL-compatible POSIX shell implementation using installed GNU utilities.
Added safe staging, empty-output validation, restrictive permissions, recursive regular-file handling, and explicit unsafe-symlink rejection.
Created a root-only rollback copy at bin/export.pre-repair.
Verified two nested files, four redactions, zero remaining emails, zero unredacted auth_token values, and zero exported symlinks.
Restarted node1 safely and verified a changed boot identity and full exporter recovery.
Removed temporary test bundles and diagnostics.

evidence.requirement: Retain timestamps, event types, and ticket IDs while redacting every email and auth_token value
evidence.summary: Exports retained the 2026-10-01 timestamps, login/update event types, and T100/T101 ticket IDs. Both auth_token keys were redacted, all four sensitive values were replaced, and no email addresses remained.

evidence.requirement: Include nested logs and reject symlinks leading outside logs/
evidence.summary: Baseline showed archive/events.log and private-link -> ../private.txt. Verification included the nested file, emitted the rejection notice, omitted private-link, and produced zero output symlinks.

evidence.requirement: Source logs and private sibling file remain unchanged
evidence.summary: Pre-change and final SHA-256 hashes match for app.log, archive/events.log, and private.txt.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: Node1 remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64; the exporter uses the existing POSIX shell and installed GNU utilities.

Captured a healthy baseline with boot ID 24d7af09-d9dc-453c-9bbd-d48f7dc4eb4e, received safe reboot acknowledgement, observed the node unavailable during restart, then confirmed new boot ID 66adc9ed-881e-450f-af42-c714f4c336c5, running system state, unchanged program/data hashes, and successful privacy-safe export recovery.
